reason: Trigger is real and fresh: a $100M Series C led by Sofina with Peak XV Partners and existing investors Balderton, Accel, ICONIQ, Tencent and Speedinvest, announced by Business Wire on 19 May 2026 (one day before the row), earmarked for AI payments and US expansion (up to 50 US hires; US to exceed one third of revenue by 2028). Primer is not a partner of any F1 or FE team and the decision path is verified (Gabriel Le Roux, Co-Founder & CEO; Pierre-Edouard Jumel, CFO; Mikael Minvielle, COO; Alex Mallet, CTO; Jade Maitland, VP Marketing; no CMO). Scored honestly it does not clear the 70 threshold: 65/100 = timing 17 (trigger 19 May; Monaco and the British GP inside the window), capacity 11 ($100M round, $170M total funding, valuation not disclosed and last set at $425M in October 2021, 274 employees, a 2023 convertible loan taken to extend runway, and the raise earmarked for hiring), brand fit 12 (B2B payments infrastructure sold to merchant finance and engineering teams; a London brand with no US identity yet; the SaaS-startup archetype 1440 has been told to stop over-indexing on), urgency 13 (US expansion is a genuine brand-build motive, but with no listing signal and no capital event beyond the round), ops fit 12 (taxonomy E2: payment orchestration for a team's store, ticketing and hospitality checkout is a real but small workstream; product_to_need 4, slot 4, on_camera 1, lock_in 3). The grid is also crowded in its lane: Visa (Red Bull, Racing Bulls), Mastercard and Airwallex (McLaren), Cash App (Racing Bulls), MoneyGram (Haas), Coinbase, Circle and CoinPayments (Aston Martin), Revolut (Audi), Barclays (Williams), eToro and Mobilize (Alpine), Nu (Mercedes); only Ferrari and Cadillac are open on payments, both at partner prices above a $100M-round company's reach. The desk scan logged Primer three times on 20 May 2026 (spec §9.4); this screen-out covers all three rows. What would change the verdict: a disclosed valuation of $1B or more, a named US headquarters or launch partner, or a US revenue share that makes a US-team partnership a budget line rather than a hope. Revisit in 2027 when US revenue is reported.
